oil_and_filter_change.title: Understanding Your Oil & Filter Change
oil_and_filter_change.summary: Engine oil lubricates and protects internal engine components, while the oil filter removes contaminants from the circulating oil.
symptoms: the oil-change interval is due
the maintenance reminder is displayed
the engine oil is dirty or degraded
oil_and_filter_change.delay_risk: Delaying this service can allow contaminated or degraded oil to circulate through the engine, increasing wear and the risk of sludge buildup.
oil_and_filter_change.customer_note: The correct oil type, viscosity, filter, and service interval depend on the vehicle manufacturer’s requirements and operating conditions.

aftercare.title: After Your Oil & Filter Change
aftercare.what_to_expect: The engine should operate normally after service. A small amount of residual oil near the filter or drain area may be cleaned during service and should not continue dripping.
care_tips: Check the oil level periodically on level ground using the manufacturer’s procedure.
Follow the next oil-change interval recommended for the vehicle and driving conditions.
Watch for fresh oil spots under the vehicle.
Use the correct oil specification and viscosity for future top-offs.
contact_shop_if: the oil-pressure warning light appears
fresh oil is leaking under the vehicle
the engine develops new ticking or knocking noises
the oil level drops noticeably soon after service

front_brake_pads_replacement.title: Understanding Your Front Brake Pad Service
front_brake_pads_replacement.summary: Brake pads press against the brake rotors to create the friction needed to slow and stop the vehicle.
symptoms: the brake pads are worn below a safe thickness
squealing or grinding is present
braking performance or pedal feel has changed
front_brake_pads_replacement.delay_risk: Continuing to drive with worn brake pads may increase stopping distance and can damage the brake rotors or other braking components.
front_brake_pads_replacement.customer_note: Final repair needs depend on inspection of the pads, rotors, calipers, hardware, and related braking components.

aftercare.title: Caring for Your New Front Brake Pads
aftercare.what_to_expect: New brake pads may require a short break-in period. Braking may feel slightly different while the pads and rotors establish an even contact surface.
care_tips: Avoid repeated hard braking during the initial break-in period unless required for safety.
Allow extra following distance while becoming familiar with the brake pedal feel.
Follow any break-in instructions provided by the shop or brake-part manufacturer.
Have the brakes inspected if noise or vibration does not improve.
contact_shop_if: the brake pedal feels unusually soft or continues sinking
the vehicle pulls strongly while braking
a brake warning light appears
grinding, severe vibration, smoke, or a burning odor develops

battery_replacement.title: Understanding Your Battery Replacement
battery_replacement.summary: The vehicle battery stores electrical energy for starting the engine and supports electrical systems when additional power is needed.
symptoms: the engine cranks slowly
the battery fails a load or capacity test
the vehicle has repeated low-voltage or no-start concerns
battery_replacement.delay_risk: A weak battery may eventually leave the vehicle unable to start and can place additional strain on the charging and starting systems.
battery_replacement.customer_note: Battery replacement should be based on battery testing and inspection of the terminals, cables, grounds, and charging system.

aftercare.title: After Your Battery Replacement
aftercare.what_to_expect: The vehicle should start normally after replacement. Some vehicles may need to relearn idle, clock, radio, window, or other electronic settings.
care_tips: Keep the battery terminals clean and securely fastened.
Avoid leaving lights or accessories on while the engine is off.
Drive the vehicle long enough for the charging system to replenish the battery after repeated short trips.
Have the charging system tested if starting becomes slow again.
contact_shop_if: the engine cranks slowly or will not start
the battery or charging warning light appears
electrical systems flicker or reset repeatedly
corrosion or swelling develops around the battery

alternator_replacement.title: Understanding Your Alternator Replacement
alternator_replacement.summary: The alternator supplies electrical power while the engine is running and recharges the vehicle battery.
symptoms: the battery or charging warning light is on
charging voltage is below specification
lights dim or electrical systems weaken while driving
alternator_replacement.delay_risk: A failing alternator may allow the battery to discharge while driving, which can cause the engine to stall or prevent the vehicle from restarting.
alternator_replacement.customer_note: The battery, drive belt, tensioner, wiring, grounds, and charging output should be checked before alternator replacement is confirmed.

aftercare.title: After Your Alternator Replacement
aftercare.what_to_expect: Charging voltage and electrical operation should return to normal after replacement. The battery may still require charging or testing if it was deeply discharged.
care_tips: Watch the instrument panel for a battery or charging warning light.
Avoid unnecessary electrical loads if the vehicle shows any charging concern.
Keep battery terminals and charging-system connections clean and tight.
Have the battery tested if it was repeatedly discharged before the alternator repair.
contact_shop_if: the battery or charging warning light returns
headlights dim or electrical systems weaken while driving
the engine stalls or the vehicle will not restart
a burning smell, belt noise, or unusual alternator noise develops

spark_plug_replacement_4_cyl.title: Understanding Your Spark Plug Service
spark_plug_replacement_4_cyl.summary: Spark plugs ignite the air-and-fuel mixture inside the engine cylinders so the engine can run smoothly and efficiently.
symptoms: the manufacturer’s replacement interval is due
the engine has a misfire or rough idle
fuel economy or acceleration has declined
spark_plug_replacement_4_cyl.delay_risk: Worn or fouled spark plugs can contribute to misfires, reduced fuel economy, hard starting, and possible catalytic-converter damage.
spark_plug_replacement_4_cyl.customer_note: Misfires can also be caused by ignition coils, fuel injectors, vacuum leaks, compression problems, or other faults, so diagnosis may still be required.

aftercare.title: After Your Spark Plug Replacement
aftercare.what_to_expect: The engine should start, idle, and accelerate smoothly after service. Fuel economy improvements may take several drive cycles to become noticeable.
care_tips: Use the fuel grade recommended by the vehicle manufacturer.
Address any returning misfire warning light promptly.
Keep future ignition-service intervals based on the manufacturer’s schedule.
Avoid ignoring rough running, hard starting, or reduced acceleration.
contact_shop_if: the check-engine light flashes
the engine misfires, shakes, or loses power
hard starting or poor acceleration continues
fuel odor or unusual exhaust smoke appears

thermostat_replacement.title: Understanding Your Thermostat Replacement
thermostat_replacement.summary: The thermostat regulates coolant flow so the engine reaches and maintains its proper operating temperature.
symptoms: the engine takes too long to warm up
the engine overheats
the coolant temperature is outside the expected range
thermostat_replacement.delay_risk: A thermostat that is stuck open can reduce heater performance and efficiency, while one that is stuck closed can cause overheating and engine damage.
thermostat_replacement.customer_note: Cooling-system concerns may also involve coolant level, air pockets, the water pump, radiator, cooling fans, sensors, or leaks.

aftercare.title: After Your Thermostat Replacement
aftercare.what_to_expect: The engine should reach and maintain normal operating temperature. Cabin heat and temperature-gauge behavior may become more consistent.
care_tips: Check the coolant level only when the engine is completely cool.
Watch the temperature gauge during the first several drives.
Use only the correct coolant type for future top-offs.
Look for fresh coolant near the thermostat housing or under the vehicle.
contact_shop_if: the engine temperature rises above normal
the coolant level drops
steam, coolant odor, or visible leakage appears
the heater suddenly blows cold while the engine is hot

water_pump_replacement.title: Understanding Your Water Pump Replacement
water_pump_replacement.summary: The water pump circulates coolant through the engine, radiator, and related cooling-system components.
symptoms: coolant is leaking near the water pump
the engine is overheating
the pump bearing is noisy or has excessive play
water_pump_replacement.delay_risk: A failing water pump can cause rapid coolant loss or loss of circulation, which may lead to severe engine overheating.
water_pump_replacement.customer_note: The entire cooling system should be inspected because leaks, thermostat faults, radiator restrictions, cooling-fan problems, and air pockets can create similar symptoms.

aftercare.title: After Your Water Pump Replacement
aftercare.what_to_expect: Coolant circulation should return to normal after repair. Minor trapped air may work through the cooling system, but overheating or continued coolant loss is not normal.
care_tips: Check the coolant level when the engine is fully cool.
Monitor the temperature gauge during the first several trips.
Inspect the parking area for fresh coolant spots.
Use the manufacturer-specified coolant for any future top-off.
contact_shop_if: the engine overheats or the temperature gauge rises
coolant continues to leak or the level drops
a grinding, whining, or belt noise develops
steam or a strong coolant odor appears

radiator_replacement.title: Understanding Your Radiator Replacement
radiator_replacement.summary: The radiator removes heat from the engine coolant before the coolant returns to the engine.
symptoms: the radiator is leaking
the engine overheats
coolant flow through the radiator is restricted
radiator_replacement.delay_risk: A leaking or restricted radiator can cause coolant loss and overheating, which may result in major engine damage.
radiator_replacement.customer_note: Radiator replacement should be confirmed by inspection and cooling-system testing because thermostats, pumps, fans, hoses, and engine concerns can produce similar symptoms.

aftercare.title: After Your Radiator Replacement
aftercare.what_to_expect: The cooling system should maintain normal engine temperature without visible leakage. Any remaining air in the system should be removed during service.
care_tips: Monitor the coolant level only when the engine is completely cool.
Watch the temperature gauge during the first several drives.
Check beneath the vehicle for fresh coolant.
Keep the radiator and grille area free of heavy debris that can block airflow.
contact_shop_if: the engine overheats
coolant leaks or the level drops
steam or a sweet coolant odor appears
the cooling fans do not operate when the engine becomes hot

tire_rotation.title: Understanding Your Tire Rotation
tire_rotation.summary: Tire rotation changes the position of the tires to help distribute tread wear more evenly.
symptoms: the scheduled rotation interval is due
front and rear tires are wearing at different rates
uneven tread wear is beginning to develop
tire_rotation.delay_risk: Skipping rotations can shorten tire life and may allow uneven wear patterns to become more severe.
tire_rotation.customer_note: Rotation does not correct alignment, suspension, inflation, balancing, or tire-damage concerns. Those conditions require separate inspection.

aftercare.title: After Your Tire Rotation
aftercare.what_to_expect: The vehicle may feel slightly different because the tires are now in different positions. Ride and steering should remain stable without new vibration.
care_tips: Check and adjust tire pressure when the tires are cold.
Recheck wheel-lug torque if the shop or vehicle manufacturer recommends it.
Continue rotating tires at the recommended interval.
Have alignment or suspension inspected if uneven wear continues.
contact_shop_if: new vibration or steering pull appears
a tire-pressure warning light remains on
a wheel or tire makes a new noise
uneven wear continues or becomes more severe

cabin_air_filter_replacement.title: Understanding Your Cabin Air Filter Replacement
cabin_air_filter_replacement.summary: The cabin air filter helps remove dust, pollen, and other airborne particles from the air entering the passenger compartment.
symptoms: airflow from the vents is weak
a musty odor is present
the maintenance interval is due
cabin_air_filter_replacement.delay_risk: A heavily restricted filter can reduce heating and air-conditioning airflow and may contribute to unpleasant odors inside the vehicle.
cabin_air_filter_replacement.customer_note: Weak airflow or odors can also be caused by blower, evaporator, duct, drain, or HVAC-system concerns.

aftercare.title: After Your Cabin Air Filter Replacement
aftercare.what_to_expect: Vent airflow and cabin air quality may improve after replacement. Existing odors may take time to clear if another HVAC source is present.
care_tips: Replace the cabin filter at the recommended interval or sooner in dusty conditions.
Keep leaves and debris away from the exterior air-intake area.
Use recirculation mode appropriately during heavy dust or smoke.
Address water leaks or persistent odors promptly.
contact_shop_if: airflow remains weak
a musty or burning odor continues
water enters the passenger compartment
the blower makes new or unusual noises
